method: PARAPHRASED AND HASH-ANCHORED from Indian Journal of Ophthalmology 71(9) (narrative review) 'Management and prevention of corneal graft rejection' (published online 21 August 2023). Every claim is a paraphrase backed by anchors (scripts/anchor.py): verify.py --source re-finds each anchored span in a fresh copy of the source, checks the claim's numbers against it and rejects copying. LICENCE: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 (read at Europe PMC fullTextXML <license> element for PMC10565940). The source's words are NOT reproduced here.

claims.claim: **After penetrating keratoplasty, rejection occurs in roughly 19% to 41% of grafts,** mostly in the first 1–3 years, though a 23% rate has been reported at 15 years.
claims.locator: Indian Journal of Ophthalmology 71(9) (narrative review), 'Management and prevention of corneal graft rejection', published online 21 August 2023, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10565940/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **In the Australian Corneal Graft Registry, 28% of 20,336 grafts had failed, and rejection caused 28% of those failures.**
claims.locator: Indian Journal of Ophthalmology 71(9) (narrative review), 'Management and prevention of corneal graft rejection', published online 21 August 2023, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10565940/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Endothelial keratoplasty carries less rejection risk than a full-thickness graft:** at 2 years one series reported 1% after DMEK, 12% after DSEK and 18% after penetrating keratoplasty.
claims.locator: Indian Journal of Ophthalmology 71(9) (narrative review), 'Management and prevention of corneal graft rejection', published online 21 August 2023, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10565940/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Recipient factors matter more than donor factors:** the original diagnosis (infective or traumatic scarring is worse), young age (under 40 in one large study), a repeat graft, glaucoma, corneal new vessels, recent eye surgery and anterior synechiae all raise risk.
claims.locator: Indian Journal of Ophthalmology 71(9) (narrative review), 'Management and prevention of corneal graft rejection', published online 21 August 2023, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10565940/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **A 'high-risk' cornea has new vessels in two or more quadrants extending 2 mm or more into the stroma, or has already rejected a graft.** Risk climbs with each extra vascularised quadrant.
claims.locator: Indian Journal of Ophthalmology 71(9) (narrative review), 'Management and prevention of corneal graft rejection', published online 21 August 2023, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10565940/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Loose, broken or exposed sutures irritate the eye, draw in vessels and can trigger rejection,** as can later surgery or removal of sutures.
claims.locator: Indian Journal of Ophthalmology 71(9) (narrative review), 'Management and prevention of corneal graft rejection', published online 21 August 2023, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10565940/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Most episodes come in the first six months but can occur at any time.** Symptoms are redness, blurred vision, light sensitivity or discomfort, yet almost 30% have no symptoms.
claims.locator: Indian Journal of Ophthalmology 71(9) (narrative review), 'Management and prevention of corneal graft rejection', published online 21 August 2023, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10565940/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Signs:** circumciliary injection is often first; then keratic precipitates, anterior chamber cells and flare, and segmental corneal oedema. A Khodadoust line (a wave of white cells moving across the endothelium) is pathognomonic. Raised pressure or a new epithelial defect can be the only clue, especially in children.
claims.locator: Indian Journal of Ophthalmology 71(9) (narrative review), 'Management and prevention of corneal graft rejection', published online 21 August 2023, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10565940/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **After endothelial keratoplasty, rejection is subtler:** in one DSEK series 35% had no symptoms and were picked up at routine review, so serial specular microscopy may help detect it early after DMEK.
claims.locator: Indian Journal of Ophthalmology 71(9) (narrative review), 'Management and prevention of corneal graft rejection', published online 21 August 2023, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10565940/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Herpes simplex endotheliitis can mimic rejection;** focal keratic precipitates on both host and donor endothelium, iritis and a pressure rise point to the virus.
claims.locator: Indian Journal of Ophthalmology 71(9) (narrative review), 'Management and prevention of corneal graft rejection', published online 21 August 2023, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10565940/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Outcome depends on catching it early and starting corticosteroids at once.** Topical steroids are the mainstay for every type of rejection.
claims.locator: Indian Journal of Ophthalmology 71(9) (narrative review), 'Management and prevention of corneal graft rejection', published online 21 August 2023, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10565940/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Endothelial rejection: prednisolone acetate 1% every 1–2 hours for the first few weeks, then taper slowly over 2–3 months once it settles;** consider lifelong low-dose drops in high-risk or one-eyed patients. **Other types:** 4–6 times a day, tapered over 6–8 weeks.
claims.locator: Indian Journal of Ophthalmology 71(9) (narrative review), 'Management and prevention of corneal graft rejection', published online 21 August 2023, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10565940/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **For severe endothelial rejection seen early, add intravenous steroid:** a single 500 mg methylprednisolone pulse raised reversal to 80%, against 39% with hourly topical drops alone, and one, two or three pulses worked equally well.
claims.locator: Indian Journal of Ophthalmology 71(9) (narrative review), 'Management and prevention of corneal graft rejection', published online 21 August 2023, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10565940/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Intravenous dexamethasone 100 mg has been proposed as a cheaper alternative;** a non-randomised series found better reversal than methylprednisolone 500 mg (72.3% against 45%).
claims.locator: Indian Journal of Ophthalmology 71(9) (narrative review), 'Management and prevention of corneal graft rejection', published online 21 August 2023, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10565940/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **For rejection that does not respond, intracameral triamcinolone (4 mg in 0.1 ml) is an extra option,** and an intravitreal dexamethasone implant has been used, though without randomised trial evidence.
claims.locator: Indian Journal of Ophthalmology 71(9) (narrative review), 'Management and prevention of corneal graft rejection', published online 21 August 2023, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10565940/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Supportive care as needed:** antibiotic prophylaxis, cycloplegics, lubricants and pressure-lowering drops.
claims.locator: Indian Journal of Ophthalmology 71(9) (narrative review), 'Management and prevention of corneal graft rejection', published online 21 August 2023, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10565940/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Topical corticosteroid for the first six months after keratoplasty is universal practice** and is the main reason rejection is uncommon then. Prednisolone is used most, whatever the risk or lens status; difluprednate, loteprednol and fluorometholone are alternatives.
claims.locator: Indian Journal of Ophthalmology 71(9) (narrative review), 'Management and prevention of corneal graft rejection', published online 21 August 2023, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10565940/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Keep topical steroids going long term if needed, but not systemic ones,** which carry serious risks. Long-term topical use can cause glaucoma, cataract and infection.
claims.locator: Indian Journal of Ophthalmology 71(9) (narrative review), 'Management and prevention of corneal graft rejection', published online 21 August 2023, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10565940/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **After anterior lamellar keratoplasty (DALK) only epithelial and stromal rejection can occur;** a longer steroid course helps prevent stromal rejection, and close monitoring is advised.
claims.locator: Indian Journal of Ophthalmology 71(9) (narrative review), 'Management and prevention of corneal graft rejection', published online 21 August 2023, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10565940/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **After endothelial keratoplasty, stopping steroids is itself a risk factor for rejection** (DSAEK).
claims.locator: Indian Journal of Ophthalmology 71(9) (narrative review), 'Management and prevention of corneal graft rejection', published online 21 August 2023, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10565940/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **High-risk grafts:** treat corneal new vessels (anti-VEGF, fine-needle diathermy or laser) where available, start an immunomodulator (preferably mycophenolate), and extend the steroid course. Topical cyclosporine has a limited role; topical tacrolimus 0.03% is a promising second-line option.
claims.locator: Indian Journal of Ophthalmology 71(9) (narrative review), 'Management and prevention of corneal graft rejection', published online 21 August 2023, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10565940/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Plan follow-up carefully and counsel patients,** because early detection is what makes rejection treatable.
claims.locator: Indian Journal of Ophthalmology 71(9) (narrative review), 'Management and prevention of corneal graft rejection', published online 21 August 2023, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10565940/, retrieved 2026-09-23
